identity.name: Ajamoda
identity.english_name: Slender celery / wild celery (botanical common-name usage varies)

classification.habitat: Open cultivated and disturbed habitats in suitable temperate/subtropical regions
classification.distribution: Reported from parts of South Asia; exact occurrence should be checked against an authenticated flora for the region

identification.description: Small aromatic herb of Apiaceae with finely divided foliage and small flowers arranged in umbels.
identification.whole_plant: Slender aromatic herb with delicate, finely divided leaves and terminal or axillary compound umbels.
identification.stem: Erect, slender and branched, generally grooved or angular.
identification.leaf: Alternate, finely divided, pinnate to dissected leaves; lower leaves generally more developed.
identification.flower: Small, typically white flowers arranged in compound umbels.
identification.fruit: Small dry schizocarp typical of Apiaceae, splitting into two mericarps at maturity.
identification.seed: Small aromatic mericarp; detailed diagnostic characters require authenticated pharmacognostic material.
identification.bark: Not applicable as a distinct woody character.
identification_points: Small dry schizocarp typical of Apiaceae

dosha.vata: May be useful in Vata-related digestive disturbance when appropriately used
dosha.pitta: May aggravate in excess because of Ushna/Tikshna properties

therapeutics.dose: Not specified in this educational dossier; dose depends on the authenticated drug material and preparation.
therapeutics.precautions: Use authenticated botanical material; excessive use of pungent/heating drugs may be unsuitable in some Pitta-dominant conditions.
therapeutics.contraindications: Preparation- and patient-specific; clinical use should be guided by a qualified practitioner.

reference_hubs: TDU Indian Medicinal Plants Database — Shlokas

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: Do not equate the botanical identity with Ajwain (Trachyspermum ammi); authenticated raw material is essential because vernacular names can overlap.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Ajamoda is used traditionally as an aromatic digestive drug. Botanical authentication is particularly important because related Apiaceae drugs have overlapping vernacular terminology.
modern_information.safety_notes: Educational entry; clinical use should use authenticated material and preparation-specific guidance.
sources: Standard pharmacognosy and Ayurvedic Dravyaguna references
